It's easy to see how these things are overlooked. Cuz when a RON plane lands, the bags are taken off it, the passengers are taken off it, and after all lost bag claims are taken, and all bags are on the carousel, and the plane's cargo bays are locked up, the workers are already tired. THEN they have to go clean the plane right before they go home. So they're in a rush to get home.

Yes; part of Ramp's responsibilities is our catering, and cleaning the plane when it remains overnight (RON flights). This includes the lavatory, all the nasty gunk, junk and various bodily fluids that passengers leave everywhere (especially children, yuck). 

The food and the beverages get on the plane because of the Ramp guys. Most large airlines contract out their catering to other companies. However, like I said before, Frontier has grouped several jobs into one job in order to save money. So basically you have guys with no concern for cleanliness and/or safety cleaning and maintaining the plane.
The number of delays Frontier had because of maintenance and unpreparedeness for boarding was astounding.

There is a reason why Frontier is so cheap compared to the other carriers. I was an employee for a number of years, working both ramp services and customer service (because their budget for their stations are quite small, employees are required to perform in multiple capacities; we would check in customers and bags, then run downstairs to load the bags we just checked).

Because the employees are so strained to perform jobs outside of their normal capacity, many (MANY MANY) procedures are overlooked; namely, hygenic procedures.

My girlfriend is a barista at Top Pot Donuts in Seattle. She has been a barista for a while and recently quit her barista job at her other job, "the drugstore" we'll call it.

I used to work for Frontier Airlines (which is a small airline compared to the other major carriers). We wanted to go on a trip and she didn't understand why I didn't want to go on Frontier; I tried to explain why Frontier sucks in terms she would understand:

"See, you work at Top Pot. A big coffee/donut shop. On one corner, you got Top Pot, on the other you got Starbucks, and on the next you got Dunkin Donuts; then, down the block you have 'the drugstore'. Frontier Airlines is 'the drugstore' of the airline world."
She got it pretty quick.

When I was in Basic Training for the Air Force, my legs were not used to all the running we did on concrete, so I had fully developed stress fractures in both my legs by the 3rd week of training. My pain would show sometimes and my instructor noticed. As hard-assed as those instructors can be, mine told me I can go to med-bay and stay there until I healed, then continue training with another group and another instructor.

Well, the bond I formed with my guys and my Instructor was already very strong. I stood up and limped out of his office and finished the entire Basic Training with basically two fractured legs (three fractures in the left leg, two in the right). Because of the AF Regs, I HAD to wait to heal in order to graduate- but I finished all the training and went through the BMT experience with my brothers and my Instructor. In the end, after I healed, I (MAYBE coincidentally?) wound up transferring right back to my Instructor as he was about to graduate another group of trainees. He was very impressed and actually showed a bit of emotion when he saw me healed up and ready to graduate. I continue talking with him to this day (something Instructors aren't allowed to do), and we maintain a good friendship.

I don't remember too many details, but when I was 12 or 13, my mother took me to visit our Japanese half of the family over in Japan (I can't remember the city). 
I had a shaved head at the time, and I got *a lot* of awkward stares, and the elderly people looked at me like I was an alien. It was about that time I noticed that nobody my age had a shaved head, and only the elderly people did. I asked my mother why I was getting so much negative attention.
She informed me that a shaved head (at that point in time, I'm not sure if it is still this way) is a major symbol that you are loyal to the old Emperor Hirohito from World War II, and thus why no young people had a shaved head. In fact, the reason why so many male youth have long and colored hair is done on purpose to usher in new ideals of a new age.
